content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Breakers 52-M2 and CB-01 both trip at the same moment. Nothing else changes: no other breaker opens or closes, normally-open (N.O.) breakers stay open, and Standby generator G1 is not running and does not start. A load has power only if a path of closed breakers connects it to a running source. Which loads that were running before the event have no power afterwards? A load behind an open breaker was not running. Answer with the load tags (for example CH-2), in the order they appear on the drawing from left to right, separated by commas.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
Bus 1 remains energized from Utility Service 1 through 52-M1, but CHWP-1 loses power when CB-01 trips. Bus 2 loses its source when 52-M2 trips; the normally-open 52-T cannot feed it from Bus 1. Bus E is connected to Bus 2, and G1 is not running, so its loads also lose power. CT-1 is excluded because CB-15 was already open.

FINAL ANSWER: CHWP-1, HP-2, LP-2, CRAH-4, RP-3, CH-1, DH-B, EL-2
